title: 3-Read Friday #88: The Spacing Calculator, Do Now Tweaks, and Perpendicular Bisectors
author: Craig Barton
summary: 3-Read Friday #88 is a practice-heavy issue centred on retrieval and instructional design. Lee Wheeler's Substack debut shares a free "Spacing Calculator" tool for automating expanding-interval retrieval scheduling. Jody Chan then describes small but consequential tweaks to a whole department's Do Now routines, made after they were chosen as a whole-school teaching focus at Durrington. Paul Rowlandson closes with a deep dive into teaching perpendicular bisector constructions through GeoGebra and reasoning from circle properties, rather than rote step-by-step compass procedure. Barton flags Book 6 of his Tips for Teachers series, on Checking for Understanding, tying the issue's retrieval-and-routine theme back to his own publishing project.
points: Wheeler's Spacing Calculator is framed by Barton as a genuine "cracker" of a Substack debut, tackling the practical scheduling problem that stops most teachers from actually implementing spaced retrieval systematically.
Chan's Do Now piece continues Barton's recurring interest in the Do Now as a lesson phase, this time from the angle of whole-department consistency rather than an individual teacher's technique.
Rowlandson's return is explicitly welcomed by Barton ("Paul is back!") as a continuation of his signature deep-dive style into a single maths topic -- this time perpendicular bisectors.

The issue's throughline is retrieval and routine: a scheduling tool, a whole-school routine review, and a construction topic that itself depends on building durable geometric reasoning rather than memorised steps.
quotes: Lee’s Substack debut is a cracker. He discusses the power of retrieval, the importance of spacing and - best of all - shares his Spacing Calculator!
Regular readers know that I love a conversation about the Do Now. Whilst it may be the shortest phase of any lesson, it sets the tone for all that follows.
Jody shares some tweaks her colleagues and she have made to their Do Nows that have improved their effectiveness.
One for the maths geeks. Paul is back! I love Paul's deep dives into the teaching of a topic. This time the subject is everyone's favourite. perpendicular bisectors.
Before we begin, you may want to check out my brand-new 16-part book series, The Tips for Teachers guide to. Book 6 on Checking for Understanding is now available.
